page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.large is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton-generation ARMv8 architecture. Built on dedicated Neoverse-V1 physical cores running at 2.6 GHz, the instance provisions 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). It is configured with 8.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), 32 MB of Level 3 cache, and a dedicated 118 GB NVMe SSD instance storage volume. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs are attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate stable single-threaded throughput balanced by modest total compute capacity due to its two-core footprint. Single-core performance achieves middle-tier results in stress-ng (1532.58) and Geekbench (1409.0), with competitive gzip single-threaded compression reaching 24.13 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics place in lower tiers, such as Geekbench multi-core at 2532.0 and PassMark CPU overall at 1555.68. Memory bandwidth shows average read throughput on uncached large blocks at 50.04 GB/sec, while write operations yield 20.09 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 3.16 million operations per second, and static web serving delivers 4.23 GB/sec.

The inclusion of direct-attached NVMe storage alongside dedicated Graviton cores provides strong resource efficiency for I/O-sensitive, lightweight services. While compute-intensive multi-threaded tasks and vector processing are constrained by core count and lack of AVX extensions, m7gd.large fits web serving, caching tiers, microservices, continuous integration agents, and scratch-disk staging workloads requiring low-latency local storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m7gd.large is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 cores on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs operating at 2.6 GHz, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network capability. The instance demonstrates solid single-core metrics across Geekbench (1409.0) and stress-ng (1532.58), complemented by 50.04 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. Due to its dual-core configuration, multi-threaded throughput and complex instruction processing are limited. With its balanced 1:4 core-to-memory profile and low-latency attached NVMe storage, m7gd.large serves efficiently for microservices, lightweight web servers, Redis caching nodes, and local I/O-intensive staging environments.
